role: corrects blocker 2 of evaluation_blocked_v1.json, which overstated an engineering obstacle as an unpassable one

corrects.why_not_edited: outputs are overwrite-forbidden; the original stands and this file records what it got wrong

what_i_said: blocker_2 stated that 'the pinned source closure no longer reproduces' and that working around it would mean scoring the new seeds 'in a different environment than seed 3072, which is the one thing a seed replication must not vary'.
what_was_wrong_with_it: I treated the auditor's HEAD-position check as if it were the invariant. It is a proxy for the invariant.
I reported the closure as not reproducing without testing the closure itself. 41 of its 45 files are byte-identical today; I had not checked when I wrote that.
I implied the scoring environment had materially changed. For the four files that differ, the scoring mathematics is unchanged.

supporting_file_unchanged.why_it_matters: it is where FUTURE_HORIZONS, HISTORY_TOKENS, QUERY_COUNT, DELAYS and EVAL_SEEDS are defined - the constants that actually determine what is scored

the_general_defect_this_exposes.pattern: a frozen contract asserts a POSITION or IDENTITY (a git HEAD, an import-closure member list, a trace step equal to a step counter) as a stand-in for the CONTENT invariant it actually cares about
the_general_defect_this_exposes.why_it_is_a_defect_and_not_just_strictne: a position proxy produces false alarms when unrelated work moves the position, and - worse - it short-circuits before the real content check ever runs. A HEAD mismatch stops the auditor at line 280, so the 45-file byte comparison at lines 283-308, which is the check with the actual scientific content, never executes.
third_instance_this_week: ContextWorld import closure: exact set equality over module paths, broken by a lazy-import refactor that changed no behaviour
loss trace terminal step: last recorded row must equal trainer.global_step, unsatisfiable by the frozen recipe's own intentional stop
source rebind HEAD pin: HEAD must equal a specific commit, broken by 12 unrelated commits
the_general_defect_this_exposes.note: in all three cases the fix was to satisfy the content invariant rather than to weaken the guard. That remains the rule; what changes is which quantity the guard should be reading.

what_this_correction_does_NOT_change.blocker_1_summary: the Development release is one-use and already consumed by seed 3072; it was built checkpoint-blind, and that blindness is what gives the seed-3072 numbers their value. Re-consuming it would retroactively weaken the result already on record.
